chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from some of his companions, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, who said:
"Intentional killing is every case in which one deliberately meant the blow; in it there is qiṣāṣ. Error is only that he intends a thing but strikes other than it."
And he said: "If he confesses against himself to the killing, he is to be killed, even if there is no evidence against him."

key_terms.الضَّرْبَ: the striking or blow intended by the killer
key_terms.الْخَطَأُ: mistaken killing; unintentionally striking someone other than the intended target
key_terms.الْقَوَدُ: retaliatory execution; qiṣāṣ for intentional killing
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: formal legal proof or evidentiary testimony
key_terms.قَتْلُ الْعَمْدِ: intentional killing; homicide done with deliberate intent

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith define intentional murder, accidental killing, and confession in qiṣāṣ cases?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the distinction between intentional killing and mistaken killing in the context of qiṣāṣ and diyāt. It also states that a valid self-confession to murder is sufficient for legal retaliation, even in the absence of external proof.
